১০) The sensory organ of hearing is situated on
Physiology-05.exp:
The correct answer is basilar membrane. The organ of Corti, which is the sensory organ of hearing, is located on the basilar membrane inside the cochlea.

Key points:

  • Basilar membrane → Supports Organ of Corti → Hearing receptor ✓

  • Hair cells of the organ of Corti convert sound vibrations into nerve impulses.

The other options are incorrect because:

  • Tectorial membrane → Overlies the organ of Corti and helps stimulate hair cells, but is not the site where the sensory organ is situated.

  • Vestibular membrane (Reissner’s membrane) → Separates scala vestibuli and scala media; not involved in housing the hearing receptor.

  • Spiral membrane → Not the standard anatomical term for the sensory organ of hearing.

High-yield Auditory physiology recall:

Organ of Corti → Basilar membrane → Cochlea → Hearing

Exam pearl:
Sensory organ of hearing = Organ of Corti, located on the basilar membrane.

Physiology-05.question: ১১) Which one is concerned with converting recent memory to long term memory?
Physiology-05.exp:
The correct answer is Hippocampus. The hippocampus plays a key role in converting short-term (recent) memories into long-term memories (memory consolidation).

Key functions:

  • Hippocampus ✓

    • Formation of new memories

    • Consolidation of short-term memory into long-term memory

    • Spatial memory

The other options are incorrect because:

  • Amygdala → Processes emotions, especially fear and emotional memory.

  • Putamen → Involved in motor control and procedural learning.

  • Pallidum (globus pallidus) → Part of basal ganglia; involved in movement regulation.

High-yield Neuro memory recall:

Hippocampus → Recent memory → Long-term memory conversion
Amygdala → Emotional memory
Basal ganglia → Motor learning

Exam pearl:
Damage to hippocampus causes inability to form new long-term memories (anterograde amnesia).

Physiology-05.question: ১২) Substances causing sour or salt tastes are mostly
১৩) Nerves concerned with taste pathway excludes
১৪) Which lens is used in astigmatism?
১৫) Contraction of medial rectus helps in accommodation of eye by
১৬) Receptors for pain-
Physiology-05.exp:
The correct answer is nociceptor. Nociceptors are specialized sensory receptors responsible for detecting painful stimuli and transmitting pain signals.

Types of stimuli detected:

  • Mechanical injury

  • Extreme temperature

  • Chemical irritation

The other options are incorrect because:

  • Mechanoreceptors → Detect mechanical sensations such as touch, pressure, and vibration.

  • Proprioceptors → Detect body position, muscle stretch, and movement.

  • Thermoreceptors → Detect temperature changes (warmth and cold).

High-yield Sensory receptor recall:

Receptor Function
Nociceptor Pain
Mechanoreceptor Touch, pressure, vibration
Thermoreceptor Temperature
Proprioceptor Position & movement

Exam pearl:
Pain sensation is mediated by nociceptors (free nerve endings).

Physiology-05.question: ১৭) Receptors are those in the rods and cones in the retina that respond to light are-
Physiology-05.exp:
The correct answer is photoreceptors. Rods and cones in the retina are photoreceptor cells that detect light and convert it into electrical signals.

Types of retinal photoreceptors:

  • Rods ✓

    • Dim light vision (scotopic vision)

    • Black and white vision

  • Cones ✓

    • Bright light vision (photopic vision)

    • Colour vision and visual acuity

The other options are incorrect because:

  • Mechanoreceptors → Detect mechanical stimuli such as touch, pressure, and vibration.

  • Proprioceptors → Detect body position and muscle movement.

  • Chemoreceptors → Detect chemical changes (e.g., taste, smell, blood gases).

High-yield Sensory receptor recall:

Receptor Stimulus
Photoreceptor Light (rods & cones)
Mechanoreceptor Touch/pressure
Thermoreceptor Temperature
Chemoreceptor Chemicals
Nociceptor Pain

Exam pearl:
Rods and cones = retinal photoreceptors responsible for vision.

Physiology-05.question: ১৮) Neurotransmitter degrading enzyme locate in
Physiology-05.exp:
The correct answer is synaptic cleft. Neurotransmitter-degrading enzymes are mainly located in the synaptic cleft, where they break down neurotransmitters to terminate their action.

Examples:

  • Acetylcholinesterase (AChE) → Located in the synaptic cleft

    • Breaks down acetylcholine into acetate and choline.

The other options are incorrect because:

  • Presynaptic membrane → Site of neurotransmitter release, not degradation.

  • Postsynaptic membrane → Contains receptors for neurotransmitters.

  • Postganglionic neuron → Transmits signals but is not the main site of neurotransmitter breakdown.

High-yield Neurotransmission recall:

Synapse:

  • Presynaptic terminal → Releases neurotransmitter

  • Synaptic cleft → Enzymatic degradation (e.g., AChE)

  • Postsynaptic membrane → Receptors

Exam pearl:
Acetylcholinesterase is present in the synaptic cleft and terminates acetylcholine action.

Physiology-05.question: ১৯) Structural and functional unit of nervous system
Physiology-05.exp:
The correct answer is Neuron. The neuron is the structural and functional unit of the nervous system because it receives, processes, and transmits nerve impulses.

Structure of a neuron:

  • Cell body (soma) → Metabolic centre

  • Dendrites → Receive signals

  • Axon → Transmit nerve impulses

The other options are incorrect because:

  • Neurotransmitter → Chemical messenger involved in communication between neurons.

  • Neuroglial cell → Provides support, protection, nutrition, and insulation for neurons but does not transmit nerve impulses as the primary unit.

  • Nerve fiber → An axon or group of axons; it is only a part of a neuron.

High-yield Neuro recall:

Structural & functional unit of nervous system → Neuron
Supporting cells → Neuroglia

Exam pearl:
Neuron = basic structural and functional unit of the nervous system.

Physiology-05.question: ২০) Neuroglial cell of PNS
Physiology-05.exp:
The correct answer is Schwann cell (Neurolemmocyte). Schwann cells are the neuroglial cells of the peripheral nervous system (PNS) and form myelin around peripheral nerves.

Neuroglial cells:

PNS:

  • Schwann cell ✓ → Myelin formation in peripheral nerves

  • Satellite cells → Support neuron cell bodies in ganglia

CNS:

  • Oligodendrocytes → Myelin formation in CNS

  • Astrocytes → Structural support, blood–brain barrier

  • Ependymal cells → Line ventricles and central canal

The other options are incorrect because:

  • Oligodendrocyte → CNS myelin-forming cell.

  • Astrocyte → CNS supporting glial cell.

  • Ependymal cell → CNS ventricular lining cell.

High-yield Neuro recall:

Location Neuroglial cell
PNS myelin Schwann cell
CNS myelin Oligodendrocyte
CNS support Astrocyte
Ventricular lining Ependymal cell

Exam pearl:
Schwann cell = PNS glial cell responsible for myelination.

Physiology-05.question: ২১) Basal nuclei excludes
Physiology-05.exp:
The correct answer is Emboliform. The emboliform nucleus is a deep cerebellar nucleus, not a basal nucleus.

Components associated with basal nuclei (basal ganglia):

  • Corpus striatum ✓

    • Caudate nucleus + Putamen

  • Amygdaloid nucleus ✓ (often included as a related basal forebrain nuclear group)

  • Claustrum ✓ (traditionally included among basal nuclei)

Emboliform nucleus ✗

  • Part of the deep cerebellar nuclei

  • Located in the cerebellum

  • Associated with coordination of movement

High-yield Neuro recall:

Deep cerebellar nuclei:

  • Dentate

  • Emboliform

  • Globose

  • Fastigial
    (Mnemonic: “Don’t Eat Greasy Food”)

Basal nuclei:

  • Caudate nucleus

  • Putamen

  • Globus pallidus

  • Claustrum

  • Amygdaloid nucleus

Exam pearl:
Emboliform = cerebellar nucleus, not basal nucleus.

Physiology-05.question: ২২) Lesion of left optic nerve results in
২৩) Not a part of visual pathway
২৪) Post ganglionic neurotransmitter of sympathetic division
২৭) Thirst and hunger control center-
Physiology-05.exp:
The correct answer is lateral hypothalamic area. The lateral hypothalamus acts as the feeding and thirst centre, stimulating hunger and water intake.

Functions:

  • Lateral hypothalamic area ✓

    • Hunger centre

    • Thirst centre

    • Lesion → Loss of appetite (aphagia) and reduced water intake

The other options are incorrect because:

  • Medial hypothalamic area → Satiety centre (controls stopping of food intake).

  • Anterior hypothalamic area → Mainly involved in heat loss mechanisms (parasympathetic responses).

  • Posterior hypothalamic area → Heat conservation and sympathetic responses.

High-yield Hypothalamus recall:

Area Function
Lateral hypothalamus Hunger + thirst centre
Ventromedial nucleus Satiety centre
Anterior hypothalamus Heat loss
Posterior hypothalamus Heat conservation

Exam pearl:
Lateral hypothalamus = “feeding centre” + thirst centre.

Physiology-05.question: ২৮) Tract carries pain and temperature from opposite side
Physiology-05.exp:
The correct answer is spinothalamic tract. The spinothalamic tract carries pain and temperature sensations from the opposite (contralateral) side of the body to the brain.

Pathway:

  • Pain & temperature receptors → Dorsal root ganglion

  • Synapse in dorsal horn of spinal cord

  • Fibres cross to the opposite side through anterior white commissure

  • Ascend via spinothalamic tract → Thalamus → Cortex

The other options are incorrect because:

  • Dorsal column → Carries fine touch, vibration, and proprioception; crosses in the medulla.

  • Corticospinal tract → Motor pathway for voluntary movement.

  • Geniculocalcarine tract (optic radiation) → Visual pathway from lateral geniculate body to visual cortex.

High-yield Neuro recall:

Tract Function Crossing
Spinothalamic tract Pain & temperature Spinal cord
Dorsal column Fine touch, vibration, proprioception Medulla
Corticospinal tract Motor Medulla

Exam pearl:
Pain + temperature from opposite side → Spinothalamic tract.

Physiology-05.question: ২৯) Most important characteristic of synaptic transmission-
Physiology-05.exp:
The correct answer is one-way conduction. The most important characteristic of synaptic transmission is that it is unidirectional, allowing impulses to pass only from the presynaptic neuron to the postsynaptic neuron.

Why?

  • Neurotransmitter is released from the presynaptic terminal

  • Receptors are present on the postsynaptic membrane

  • Therefore, transmission occurs in one direction only ✓

The other options are incorrect because:

  • Excitation → Synapses may be excitatory or inhibitory; not the defining feature.

  • Synaptic delay → A characteristic feature (about 0.5 ms) but not the most important.

  • Summation → A property of synaptic integration, not the primary characteristic.

High-yield Neuro recall:

Major characteristics of synaptic transmission:

  • One-way conduction ⭐

  • Synaptic delay

  • Summation

  • Facilitation

  • Fatigue

Exam pearl:
Synapse allows transmission in only one direction: presynaptic → postsynaptic.

Physiology-05.question: ৩০) Nerve fiber for slow pain
Physiology-05.exp:
The correct answer is Type C nerve fibres. Slow pain (dull, aching, burning pain) is transmitted by small, unmyelinated Type C fibres.

Pain fibre classification:

  • Type C fibres ✓

    • Slow pain

    • Dull, aching, burning sensation

    • Unmyelinated

    • Slow conduction velocity

  • Aδ fibres → Fast pain (sharp, pricking pain); thinly myelinated

  • Aβ fibres → Touch, pressure, vibration

  • Aα fibres → Motor function and proprioception

High-yield Sensory fibre recall:

Fibre Function
Aδ Fast/sharp pain
C Slow/dull pain
Aβ Touch & pressure
Aα Motor & proprioception

Exam pearl:
Slow pain = Type C fibre = Unmyelinated.

Physiology-05.question: ৩১) Neurotransmitter of Fast pain-
Physiology-05.exp:
The correct answer is Glutamate. Fast pain (first pain) transmitted by Aδ fibres uses glutamate as the main neurotransmitter.

Pain pathway neurotransmitters:

  • Fast pain (Aδ fibres) → Glutamate ✓

    • Sharp, pricking, well-localized pain

    • Rapid conduction due to myelination

  • Slow pain (C fibres) → Substance P

    • Dull, burning, poorly localized pain

    • Slow conduction

The other options are incorrect because:

  • Substance P → Mainly involved in slow pain transmission.

  • Serotonin → Modulates pain pathways in the CNS.

  • Acetylcholine → Neurotransmitter in neuromuscular junction and autonomic pathways.

High-yield Pain pathway recall:

Pain type Fibre Neurotransmitter
Fast pain Aδ fibre Glutamate
Slow pain C fibre Substance P

Exam pearl:
Aδ fibre → Glutamate → Fast sharp pain
C fibre → Substance P → Slow burning pain.

৪৩) Presbycusis is –
Physiology-05.exp:
The correct answer is age-related hearing impairment. Presbycusis is a progressive, bilateral sensorineural hearing loss that occurs due to ageing.

Key features:

  • Usually affects high-frequency sounds first

  • Due to degeneration of:

    • Cochlear hair cells

    • Spiral ganglion neurons

    • Stria vascularis

The other options are incorrect because:

  • Age-related vision impairment → Presbyopia (difficulty focusing near objects).

  • Age-related balance impairment → Related to vestibular system degeneration.

  • Age-related memory impairment → Age-associated cognitive decline.

High-yield ENT recall:

Term Meaning
Presbycusis Age-related hearing loss
Presbyopia Age-related loss of near vision
Presbyosmia Age-related loss of smell

Exam pearl:
Presbycusis = elderly + bilateral sensorineural deafness.

Physiology-05.question: ৪৪) Vestibular ganglion is first order neuron of
Physiology-05.exp:
The correct answer is balance. The vestibular ganglion (Scarpa’s ganglion) contains the first-order neurons of the vestibular pathway, which is responsible for balance and equilibrium.

Pathway:

  • Vestibular receptors (semicircular canals, utricle, saccule)
    → Vestibular ganglion (first-order neuron)
    → Vestibular nuclei in brainstem
    → Cerebellum and other centres

The other options are incorrect because:

  • Vision → First-order neuron is in the retina (retinal ganglion cells).

  • Taste → First-order neurons are in sensory ganglia of CN VII, IX, and X.

  • Smell → First-order neurons are olfactory receptor cells in the nasal epithelium.

High-yield Neuro recall:

System First-order neuron location
Balance (vestibular) Vestibular ganglion (Scarpa)
Hearing Spiral ganglion
Taste Geniculate/petrosal/nodose ganglia
Smell Olfactory receptor cells

Exam pearl:
Vestibular ganglion = first-order neuron of balance pathway.

Physiology-05.question: ৪৫) Medial geniculate body involve in
Physiology-05.exp:
The correct answer is hearing. The medial geniculate body (MGB) is the relay nucleus of the auditory pathway in the thalamus.

Auditory pathway:

  • Cochlea → Cochlear nerve (CN VIII)

  • Cochlear nuclei

  • Superior olivary nucleus

  • Inferior colliculus

  • Medial geniculate body ✓

  • Primary auditory cortex (temporal lobe)

The other options are incorrect because:

  • Vision ✗ → Involves the lateral geniculate body (LGB).

  • Taste ✗ → Involves nucleus of solitary tract and thalamic taste pathways.

  • Smell ✗ → Olfactory pathway bypasses the thalamus initially.

High-yield Thalamic nuclei recall:

Thalamic nucleus Function
Lateral geniculate body Vision
Medial geniculate body Hearing
Ventral posterolateral nucleus Body sensation
Ventral posteromedial nucleus Face sensation

Exam pearl:
Medial = Music (hearing), Lateral = Light (vision).

Physiology-05.question: ৪৬) Receptors for Taste sensation (Taste bud) is -
Physiology-05.exp:
The correct answer is chemoreceptor. Taste buds contain specialized gustatory receptor cells that detect dissolved chemical substances in food.

Taste receptor mechanism:

  • Food chemicals dissolve in saliva

  • Bind to receptors on taste receptor cells

  • Generate nerve signals through cranial nerves VII, IX, and X

The other options are incorrect because:

  • Mechanoreceptors → Detect mechanical stimuli such as touch, pressure, and vibration.

  • Photoreceptors → Detect light (rods and cones in retina).

  • Thermoreceptors → Detect temperature changes.

High-yield Sensory receptor recall:

Receptor Stimulus
Chemoreceptor Taste & smell (chemical stimuli)
Photoreceptor Light
Mechanoreceptor Touch/pressure
Thermoreceptor Temperature
Nociceptor Pain

Exam pearl:
Taste bud = Chemoreceptor detecting dissolved chemicals.
